atlas_techniques.name: Valid Accounts
atlas_techniques.mechanism: JWT + OAuth2 + API key auth enforced on MCP data path; WebAuthn/FIDO2 MFA on admin management interface (M007)
atlas_techniques.notes: Auth layer active for all MCP traffic. WebAuthn/FIDO2 MFA shipped M007 for admin dashboard. MCP data path uses JWT/API key — MFA applies to the management plane, not per-request MCP sessions.

atlas_techniques.name: Denial of ML Service
atlas_techniques.mechanism: Per-identity rate limiting (JWT subject / API-key keyed, LRU-bounded) shipped M007; per-IP fallback for unauthenticated sessions
atlas_techniques.notes: Identity-keyed rate limiting shipped M007 — authenticated requests bucketed by JWT subject / API key, not IP. LRU cap prevents unbounded memory growth under IP rotation. Unauthenticated sessions fall back to per-IP bucket (spoofable via X-Forwarded-For behind proxies — see SECURITY.md).

atlas_techniques.name: Execute LLM Prompt
atlas_techniques.mechanism: JWT auth enforced on all MCP endpoints; unauthenticated requests return 401 (ISC-66)

atlas_techniques.name: Direct Prompt Injection
atlas_techniques.mechanism: 22+ active patterns post-normalisation via IOC trie; case/spacing/unicode normalisation applied pre-match
atlas_techniques.notes: IOC patterns wired and pre-compiled at startup (ISC-7, ISC-8 confirmed). Pattern count: 61 IOC patterns active.

atlas_techniques.name: Indirect Prompt Injection (via tool results)
atlas_techniques.mechanism: detectPromptInjection() to be applied to tool call results before forwarding (M008, ISC-22)
atlas_techniques.notes: Currently not scanned. Tool call response bodies are a distinct unscanned surface. Planned in M008.

atlas_techniques.name: Triggered Injection
atlas_techniques.mechanism: IOC pattern active post-M006; triggered injection pattern detected
atlas_techniques.notes: Covered by active IOC pattern set (ISC-47).

atlas_techniques.name: Agent Tool Invocation Abuse
atlas_techniques.mechanism: validateResourceURI() on URL-typed tool arguments (ISC-12 confirmed)
atlas_techniques.notes: Confirmed in code: internal/server/mcp_proxy.go:800. SSRF via tool args blocked.

atlas_techniques.name: Jailbreak — DAN
atlas_techniques.notes: DAN prompt blocked by pattern detection (ISC-49).

atlas_techniques.name: System Prompt Override
atlas_techniques.notes: Roleplay/act-as pattern confirmed in code: (?i)(?:role play|act as|pretend to be) triggers detection.

atlas_techniques.name: Crescendo (Gradual Escalation)
atlas_techniques.mechanism: LLM judge layer required (M009, ISC-42, ISC-52)
atlas_techniques.notes: Structurally undetectable at transport layer. Slow multi-turn escalation without explicit keywords cannot be caught by pattern matching. Requires semantic/behavioural analysis in the judge layer. This is above the 62% ceiling.

atlas_techniques.name: Meta Prompt Extraction
atlas_techniques.mechanism: Pure extraction patterns (no override verb required) shipped M008 (ISC-25); system prompt override patterns active from M001
atlas_techniques.notes: 'what are your instructions verbatim' class patterns active. Both override-verb and pure-extraction variants covered.

atlas_techniques.name: LLM Data Leakage
atlas_techniques.mechanism: Response compliance scan active (ISC-11 confirmed); secret detection patterns partially active; Azure SAS, GCP SA JSON, Slack tokens not yet added (ISC-17 through ISC-19 pending M007)
atlas_techniques.notes: Core PII/PHI/PCI response scanning confirmed in code (internal/server/mcp_proxy.go:340). Extended secret patterns pending M007.

atlas_techniques.name: RAG Poisoning
atlas_techniques.mechanism: LLM judge layer detects intent (M009, ISC-42, ISC-55)
atlas_techniques.notes: Requires semantic intent detection above the 62% transport-layer ceiling. Planned in M009 judge layer.

atlas_techniques.name: SSRF via Tool Arguments
atlas_techniques.mechanism: Parse-time IP/hostname validation via validateResourceURI(); connection-time re-validation pending (BUG-2)
atlas_techniques.notes: ISC-1 and ISC-12 implementations correct. DNS rebinding bypass still possible (BUG-2): parse-time validation can be bypassed by attacker-controlled hostname resolving to private IP post-parse. Fix requires custom DialContext.

atlas_techniques.name: Case and Spacing Bypass
atlas_techniques.mechanism: Pre-match normalisation: case folding, spacing collapse, unicode normalisation
atlas_techniques.notes: Normalisation active on all pattern matching paths (ISC-58).

atlas_techniques.name: Leet Speak Bypass
atlas_techniques.mechanism: Leet normalisation pass before pattern matching shipped M008 (ISC-24, ISC-59)
atlas_techniques.notes: Active. ign0re all pr3v1ous 1nstruct1ons class patterns caught via pre-normalisation before Aho-Corasick trie.

not_covered: ML model weights, training pipelines, or fine-tuning infrastructure — Aegir is a transport-layer proxy
Supply chain or physical environment security
Attacks that require access to model internals or embeddings
SIEM functionality — Aegir produces audit logs suitable for SIEM ingestion; it is not a SIEM
The LLM judge's training or alignment — Aegir consumes a judge API/binary; it does not train one

Crescendo (AML.T0054.007) and session-level distributed model extraction — LLM judge (M009) handles single-turn semantic attacks but lacks cross-request session context for Crescendo detection (ISC-52 open)
Indirect prompt injection via tool results — tool result scanning against full IOC suite pending (ISC-22 open)
Network segmentation and process-level least privilege

a2a.description: Aegir cannot distinguish agent-sourced from human-sourced requests and does not provide trust verification for delegated agent authority. All requests arriving at the MCP transport layer are treated identically regardless of whether they originate from a human operator, an orchestrating agent, or a sub-agent in a delegation chain. Aegir has no mechanism to verify that a claimed agent identity is authorised to act on behalf of a principal, cannot detect authority escalation in agent delegation chains, and cannot enforce per-principal scope restrictions in multi-agent pipelines. This is a structural gap in the current architecture; closing it requires an A2A trust layer (signed delegation tokens, verified agent identity, per-principal scope enforcement) that is not planned in any current milestone.
